applicability.scope: Documenting or reviewing an optimization campaign whose verdict will be cited downstream
applicability.prerequisites: A campaign with pinned baseline and candidate SHAs and an evidence tree under evidence/<campaign-id>/; conclusions about goal authority additionally need the LoopX governance reference
applicability.input_contract: Campaign artifacts in plan/, results/, patch/ and validator/, plus the RunSpec that fixes repo x revision x backend x device x model x scenario
applicability.produced_artifact: An evidence record that links paths instead of pasting metrics, and states exactly one of PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE with its rationale
failure_modes: Metrics pasted into an issue comment with no link to an evidence path
PASS recorded on a cleanup or integrity-probe failure
Output reused across trials, aliased into a reference, or written outside its own trial directory
Source fingerprint taken over a directory overlap that excludes changed tracked files
Org-wide default SHAs assumed in a skill or CI instead of read from the acceptance issue
applicability.refusal_point: Refuses PASS when the validator freeze, the results rationale or the pinned SHAs are missing, and reports INCONCLUSIVE for that campaign instead

recommendations: Link evidence paths in the report; a metric quoted only in a comment cannot be re-checked later.
Fingerprint tracked source even when the output directory overlaps it, and exclude only the current run's generated files.
Treat a missing upstream-cache release proof as INCONCLUSIVE rather than a PASS with a caveat.
Read baseline and candidate SHAs from the acceptance issue for that campaign, never from a skill default.
limitations: Documents evidence discipline; it performs no measurement and certifies no campaign.
The LoopX goal-governance reference is a source-derived candidate and adds no execution permission or empirical validation.
